001package io.github.ai4ci.config.setup;
002
003import org.immutables.value.Value;
004import org.jgrapht.generate.BarabasiAlbertGraphGenerator;
005import org.jgrapht.graph.DefaultEdge;
006import org.jgrapht.graph.SimpleGraph;
007
008import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
009import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeName;
010import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
011import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
012
013import io.github.ai4ci.abm.Person;
014
015/**
016 * Barabasi‑Albert preferential attachment network configuration.
017 *
018 * <p>
019 * This configuration is used to generate scale‑free networks via the
020 * Barabasi‑Albert algorithm. The concrete generator is invoked during the
021 * {@code setupOutbreak} stage to populate the simulation's social graph.
022 *
023 * <p>
024 * Extension guidance: tune the degree parameter or replace the generator with a
025 * custom implementation if a different degree distribution is required.
026 *
027 * @author Rob Challen
028 */
029@Value.Immutable
030@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableBarabasiAlbertConfiguration.class)
031@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableBarabasiAlbertConfiguration.class)
032@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
033@JsonTypeName("barabasi-albert")
034public interface BarabasiAlbertConfiguration extends NetworkConfiguration {
035
036        /**
037         * Default Barabasi‑Albert configuration used in examples and tests.
038         *
039         * <p>
040         * The default values provide a compact set of parameters used in examples
041         * and tests. Downstream callers that rely on this simple default include the
042         * default setup configuration and example experiments.
043         *
044         * @see io.github.ai4ci.config.setup.SetupConfiguration#DEFAULT
045         */
046        ImmutableBarabasiAlbertConfiguration DEFAULT = ImmutableBarabasiAlbertConfiguration
047                .builder()
048                .setDescription(
049                        "A 128x128 Barbasi Albert network with on average 100 contacts per node."
050                )
051                .setNetworkSize(128 * 128)
052                .setNetworkDegree(100)
053                .build();
054
055        // Integer getMinimumDegree();
056        // Integer getMParameter();
057
058        // n is final size nodes
059        // total edges = m0*(m0-1)/2 + m*( n - m0)
060        // av degree (d) = total edges / n
061        // d*n = m0^2/2 -m0/2 + m*n - m*m0
062        // 0 = m0^2 - (1 + 2*m)*m0 + 2*(m-d)*n
063        // m*(n - m0) = - m0^2/2 + m0/2 + d*n
064        // m = (- m0^2/2 + m0/2 + d*n)/(n - m0)
065
066        // minimum degree = m0-1
067
068        /**
069         * Populate the supplied social network graph using the stored parameters.
070         *
071         * @param socialNetwork mutable graph to populate
072         */
073        @Override
074        default void generateGraph(SimpleGraph<Person, DefaultEdge> socialNetwork) {
075                int n = this.getNetworkSize();
076                var m = this.getNetworkDegree() / 2;
077                var gen = new BarabasiAlbertGraphGenerator<Person, DefaultEdge>(
078                                m, m, n
079                );
080                gen.generateGraph(socialNetwork);
081        }
082}
